sourcedFrom: Ruger Mark IV Instruction Manual — PM1179 (2026)
cleanIntro: The Mark IV comes apart without tools — one button, a tilt, and the upper lifts off. Ruger’s manual covers Standard, Target, Hunter, Competition and both 22/45 variants.

steps.title: Clear it, safety on
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction and fingers out of the trigger guard: drop the magazine and empty it, draw the bolt fully rearward, look into the chamber, release the bolt, then put the safety on with the white dot visible.
steps.prose: The white dot is the tell. If you cannot see it, the safety is not on.
steps.quote: Draw the bolt fully rearward and visually inspect the chamber to be certain that there is no cartridge in it and then release the bolt.
steps.cite: Ruger Mark IV Instruction Manual — PM1179 — Disassembly, step 1, p.21
steps.warn: Always unload a firearm before cleaning, lubrication, disassembly, or assembly.

steps.title: Press the take-down button
steps.action: Hold the barrel in one hand and the grip frame assembly in the other, and depress the take-down button just below the rear of the bolt.
steps.prose: No tools at all on this pistol — Ruger designed the Mark IV specifically so the old Mark III wrestling match is gone.
steps.quote: Holding the barrel in one hand and the grip frame assembly in the other, depress the take-down button located just below the rear of the bolt
steps.cite: Ruger Mark IV Instruction Manual — PM1179 — Disassembly, step 2, p.21

steps.title: Tilt the barrel down, lift the upper off
steps.action: With the button held in, tilt the barrel downward so it clears the bolt stop pin, then lift the barrel/receiver assembly straight up off the grip frame assembly.
steps.prose: Tilt first, then straight up. Lifting without the tilt binds on the bolt stop pin.
steps.quote: The barrel/receiver assembly can now be lifted straight up off of the grip frame assembly
steps.cite: Ruger Mark IV Instruction Manual — PM1179 — Disassembly, step 3, p.21

steps.title: Bolt out of the receiver
steps.action: Pull straight back on the bolt ears to remove the bolt from the receiver.
steps.prose: Straight back by the ears — that is the whole job.
steps.quote: Pull straight back on the bolt ears to remove the bolt from the receiver
steps.cite: Ruger Mark IV Instruction Manual — PM1179 — Disassembly, step 5, p.21

steps.title: That is the end of it
steps.action: Grips can come off with a 3/32 inch hex wrench if you want them off, but nothing else needs to.
steps.prose: Ruger says so in as many words.
steps.cite: Ruger Mark IV Instruction Manual — PM1179 — Disassembly, step 5, p.21

deepAbsentReason: PM1179 closes its disassembly with "No further disassembly is necessary." (p.21). Nothing past the field strip is documented, so this listing has NO deep clean.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Run a solvent-wet patch through the bore, then a correctly sized brush, then dry patches until clean
Rimfire fouling is waxy — expect more scrubbing than a centrefire bore needs

cleaning.name: BOLT & RECEIVER
tasks: Scrub the bolt face and the extractor recess
Wipe the receiver interior and the bolt raceways
A light film of oil on the bolt bearing surfaces, no more

cleaning.name: GRIP FRAME
tasks: Wipe the frame and the magazine well dry
Magazines stay dry — no oil where ammunition sits

reassembly: Return the bolt to the receiver, ears first.
Seat the barrel/receiver assembly onto the grip frame and swing it up until the take-down button clicks home.
Work the bolt several times before handling further.
fncheck: With the magazine out and chamber confirmed empty, check the safety blocks the trigger and the bolt runs freely, pointed in a safe direction.
